From Virginia the re-roll only forces a BW house sale on Illinois ($300, 3/36). At $160, reds 7/9/10 plus orange 1-house 4/5 are 20/36 forced sales and kill the $1400 rent. $20 more doesn't save BW3 on Illinois; p4 called $120 final, so don't risk a walk-away. Keep Vermont. message.reasoning:
I need to decide whether to accept, reject, or counter the current trade offer.

I'm p2 with four mortgaged properties and two houses on Boardwalk and Park Place. The Boardwalk monopoly is the win condition. I need at least $140 to avoid selling a house if I roll non-doubles.

Accepting the $120 offer gives me $280 cash. This is better than rolling doubles at $160, which would force a Boardwalk house sale and drop the $1400 kill.

I'm recalculating the exact board positions from Virginia Avenue. My earlier assumption about which squares land on 7, 9, and 10 was wrong. I need to verify which properties are owned by other players before deciding whether to accept the trade.

From Virginia Avenue, rolling doubles lands on Kentucky, Indiana, and Illinois. Each carries $250 or $300 rent with two houses. The probability of hitting these dangerous squares is 13 out of 36. Tennessee and New York are also reachable from here.

Tennessee and New York each carry $200 and $220 rent with one house. Rolling doubles at $160 forces a Boardwalk house sale to pay the $250 hit on Kentucky, leaving only $10. A $300 hit on Illinois would require selling two houses to stay afloat.

Accepting the $120 offer gives me $280 total. A $250 hit on Kentucky or Indiana leaves $30 cash and preserves all buildings. A $300 hit on Illinois still forces a Boardwalk house sale, dropping the kill rent to $600 but leaving $80 cash. Rolling doubles at $160 alone would force two house sales to pay the same $300 hit, leaving only $60.

I will accept the $120 offer. I have already decided to accept any counter between $100 and $139 rather than roll doubles at $160.

Rolling doubles at $160 forces a house sale on 20 of 36 outcomes. At $280 only the $300 Illinois hit would require a sale. I am now considering raising the counter to $130.

A $130 counter is too risky. p4 has already raised the offer to $120, and pushing higher could make them reject entirely. That would leave me at $160 with a 20/36 chance of forced house sales before the re-roll.

The trade also carries strategic cost. p4 would gain St. Charles, but that does not complete a pink monopoly because States is mortgaged by p1. They would also receive Water Works, completing a utility pair that would charge 10× dice rent.

p4 would pay the unmortgage cost for Water Works. Pennsylvania Railroad pairs with Reading, but that only yields $50 rent and is harmless because B&O and Short Line are still mortgaged. I keep Vermont to block a light-blue monopoly. After the trade p4 would have about $678 cash. From Virginia I cannot land on either utility this roll, so the new utility pair poses no immediate threat.

I will accept the trade and keep my public reply brief and gracious. I will not reveal the $280 buffer or re-roll math. The mortgaged properties transfer with their mortgage status intact.
